terms.grammar: orbis, orbis m., with lacteus, lactea, lacteum
evidence: Cic. Rep. 6.16: quem vōs, ut ā Grajīs accēpistis, orbem lacteum nuncupātis
terms.comment: Cicero’s name for it in Scipio’s dream, a translation of the Greek γαλαξίας κύκλος.

evidence: Ov. M. 1.168–169: Est via sublīmis, caelō manifesta serēnō; lactea nōmen habet
terms.comment: Ovid’s road of the gods across the sky; the name most modern languages translate.

evidence: Plin. NH 2.91: in candidā, quae lacteī circulī nōmen accēpit

phrases.latin: Suspice: vidēsne illum candōrem per caelum? Orbis lacteus est.
phrases.english: Look up: can you see that whiteness across the sky? It’s the Milky Way.

phrases.latin: Est via sublīmis, caelō manifesta serēnō; lactea nōmen habet, candōre notābilis ipsō.
phrases.english: There is a road on high, plain to see when the sky is clear; it is called the Milky Way, and its very whiteness marks it out.

phrases.latin: Erat autem is splendidissimō candōre inter flammās circus ēlūcēns. «Quem vōs, ut ā Grajīs accēpistis, orbem lacteum nuncupātis.»
phrases.english: It was a ring shining out among the fires with the most brilliant whiteness. “Which you, as you learned from the Greeks, call the Milky Way.”

sources: Lewis & Short: lacteus · Lewis & Short: orbis · Lewis & Short: circulus
